subject: History
description: Slave, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, Lodi dynasties

questions.stem: The DELHI SULTANATE's FIRST (Slave / Mamluk) dynasty was founded in the year:
questions.explanation: Qutb-ud-din Aibak — founded Slave / Mamluk dynasty 1206 after the death of Muhammad Ghori. Began Qutub Minar. 1192 — Second Battle of Tarain (Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan). 1290 — Khalji dynasty. 1320 — Tughlaq. 1414 — Sayyid. 1451 — Lodi. 1526 — Mughals (end of Sultanate).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: ALAUDDIN KHALJI belonged to which dynasty?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji (r. 1296-1316) — Khalji dynasty. Greatest Khalji king. Elaborate market-price reforms, southern conquests (Devagiri, Warangal, Madurai) via Malik Kafur, defended against Mongol invasions, built Alai Darwaza and Siri Fort. Died 1316. Only Khalji of exam importance.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: RAZIA SULTAN, the only woman to rule the Delhi Sultanate, belonged to which dynasty?
questions.explanation: Razia Sultan — Iltutmish's daughter, ruled Delhi 1236-1240. Slave / Mamluk dynasty. First woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. Discarded veil (unusual for era). Challenged by Turkish chiefs; deposed and killed at Kaithal in 1240.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Match the Sultan with his INNOVATION. A. Iltutmish.  B. Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq.  C. Firoz Shah Tughlaq.  D. Sikandar Lodi. List-II: 1. Introduced silver tanka + copper jital.  2. Token currency experiment.  3. Restored iqtas; dug canals; repaired Qutub Minar.  4. Established Agra as new capital (1504).
questions.explanation: Iltutmish — introduced silver tanka + copper jital (1235). Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq — token currency (copper tokens valued like silver, 1329-1331 — counterfeiting crisis). Firoz Shah Tughlaq — canals on Yamuna/Sutlej, iqta system restored, Ashoka Pillar moved to Delhi. Sikandar Lodi — founded Agra (1504).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The LAST Sultan of Delhi was:
questions.explanation: Ibrahim Lodi (r. 1517-1526) — last Sultan of Delhi. Defeated and killed by Babur at the First Battle of Panipat, 21 April 1526. End of Delhi Sultanate, beginning of Mughal rule. Sikandar Lodi (1489-1517) was his father; also founded Agra. defeated at Panipat 1526.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The famous IQTA SYSTEM of the Delhi Sultanate refers to:

options.option_text: A revenue / territorial assignment to nobles for military service

questions.explanation: Iqta — land-revenue assignment given to Sultanate nobles ('iqtadars') in lieu of cash salary. Persian origin. Initially non-hereditary and transferable; Firoz Shah Tughlaq made it de-facto hereditary. Similar to the European feudal fief. Later Mughals replaced with mansabdari + jagirdari system. like a fief.
questions.subject: History

_fixes.was: A revenue / territorial assignment to nobles for military service (like a fief)
_fixes.now: A revenue / territorial assignment to nobles for military service

questions.stem: TIMUR's invasion and sack of Delhi took place in the year:
questions.explanation: Timur (Tamerlane) — Turko-Mongol conqueror, sacked Delhi in December 1398 during Tughlaq decline. Massacred thousands, took craftsmen back to Samarkand. Delhi Sultanate never fully recovered. Sayyid dynasty ruled next (1414) as weakened successor. Babur (Timur's descendant) later founded Mughals.
